lesson.child_mission: Testing a mechanism collects data against criteria; improving means changing one feature at a time and retesting.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Your toy fails “rolls 1 m”. List two possible causes and one improvement test for each.

FEEDBACK
e.g. friction/wheels sticky → clean/lubricate carefully; axle bent → straighten — must be testable.

WATCH FOR
Changing five things between trials hides what fixed the problem.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Run at least three test–improve cycles on your mechanism. Data table + final version notes.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Run at least three test–improve cycles on your mechanism. Data table + final version notes. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: e.g. friction/wheels sticky → clean/lubricate carefully; axle bent → straighten — must be testable. Reasoning: I used test by attending to improve rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Changing five things between trials hides what fixed the problem. Correction: e.g. friction/wheels sticky → clean/lubricate carefully; axle bent → straighten — must be testable. Why: the correction restores accurate use of test.

Parent: Likely misconception: Changing five things between trials hides what fixed the problem. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses test. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about test, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Require a new example, named observations and a claim–evidence link. / Require misconception + corrected claim + evidence reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Trial table: distance rolled; straightness score. If it veers, change axle alignment only, then retest. Keep notes of each version.

TRY FIRST
Your toy fails “rolls 1 m”. List two possible causes and one improvement test for each.

FEEDBACK
e.g. friction/wheels sticky → clean/lubricate carefully; axle bent → straighten — must be testable.
teach_steps.explain:
Testing a mechanism collects data against criteria; improving means changing one feature at a time and retesting.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Changing five things between trials hides what fixed the problem. Correct the claim or method, not just the neatness of the diagram.
